segments.beat: Slower movement + lower intake → constipation and bloating
segments.copy: He explained there were a couple of things going on. GLP-1s slow stomach emptying and can slow the contractions that move food along. Then your appetite decreases. You're eating less, so you may get less fiber too. Put those together, and you've got a recipe for constipation—and that backed-up, bloated feeling.
segments.visual: S01a: Narrator recounts explanation; S01b: stomach/duodenum movement illustration; S01c: distinct side-view smaller meal and fiber-containing foods; S01d: return to narrator on bloated feeling.
segments.evidence: Podcast supplies conversational sequence, not a real Facebook quote. GLP-1 motility evidence supports general explanation. Lower fiber intake is a possibility, not universal or the first nutrient everyone cuts. No diagnosis or claim that all bloating has this cause.

microbeats.action: Stomach/duodenum illustration; show slower movement without total blockage
New smaller-meal composition; show possibility of reduced fiber intake
Narrator; land on constipation and bloated feeling

segments.copy: Fiber can help bowel regularity, and MiraLAX softens stool by holding water in it. Those jobs are different from speeding up stomach emptying. That was the distinction I'd missed.
segments.visual: S02: Separate colon/stool hydration illustration with accurate labels, then a small anatomical locator.
segments.evidence: Functional comparison after UMP. Do not generalize to fiber/MiraLAX never helping GLP-1 symptoms or the colon being innocent.

segments.copy: So my next question was: how do I address the slowdown? What should I actually look for? That became a three-part checklist.
segments.visual: F02: Narrator at kitchen table; notebook with three empty rows, no bottle/brand.
segments.evidence: Open solution question only after problem mechanism and prior-remedy distinction.

segments.copy: First, a compound from celery juice, for [the verified action relevant to stomach movement].
segments.visual: I01: Celery juice/compound macro and a plain role card; no gastric effect animation until substantiated.
segments.evidence: OPEN COPY SLOT: no reviewed human evidence establishes Motilli/apigenin accelerates stomach emptying. Do not fill with invented effect. V8 review: apigenin is a flavone, not an enzyme. Mouse-colon inflammatory and motor findings do not establish human GLP-1 gastric-emptying benefit; current product apigenin dose is unspecified. See evidence/ingredient-mechanism-review-v8.md.

segments.copy: Second, chlorophyllin, a plant-derived ingredient, for [the verified action relevant to gas or bloating].
segments.visual: I02: Distinct plant-pigment macro and ingredient form label; no gas disappearance or binding animation without matching support.
segments.evidence: OPEN COPY SLOT: gas neutralization/bloating relief at this formula/dose not established by reviewed evidence. V8 review: odor endpoints are distinct from fermentation, gas volume, or bloating; controlled odor evidence is mixed. No established fermentation-stopping role at seller-listed 0.54 mg/day. See ingredient review.

segments.copy: Third, a soluble prebiotic fiber to feed bacteria in the gut. The type and amount matter, because more fiber can mean more gas for some people.
segments.visual: I03: Distinct microscopic fiber-substrate view, restrained labels; no zero-bulk/guaranteed passage depiction.
segments.evidence: Supported general prebiotic role and tolerance qualification. Not evidence that this FOS nudges stomach contents or treats delayed emptying.

segments.beat: Combine the three after explaining them
segments.copy: Then I came across Motilli. It combines celery juice powder, chlorophyllin, and prebiotic fiber in one daily gummy, so I could review the whole formula together.
segments.visual: PR01: First actual current Motilli bottle/page reveal; three previously introduced ingredient labels surround bottle.
segments.evidence: Product identity seller-listed. Fit with the first two claimed jobs remains conditional on substantiating those exact UMS slots.

segments.copy: The directions are two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. I liked the simplicity of chewing something instead of swallowing another capsule.
segments.evidence: Seller-listed directions checked; personal preference conditional. No faster absorption or prescriber endorsement invented.
